domain.name: Sales & Customer Service
domain.description: Practical qualification, discovery, proposals, objections, closing, onboarding, service recovery, retention, and referrals.

competencies.name: Lead Qualification
competencies.description: Determine whether a prospect is worth deeper sales effort.

units.title: Qualification tests fit and readiness
units.content: Useful qualification checks problem, urgency, decision authority, budget reality, timing, and fit with the offer without forcing every lead through the same script.

units.title: Qualification workflow
units.content: Capture source and request; clarify desired outcome, timing, decision process, budget range, and constraints; identify disqualifiers; then route to nurture, discovery, quote, or decline.

units.title: Qualification failures
units.content: Avoid treating curiosity as buying intent, hiding price reality until late, chasing poor-fit work, and rejecting leads based only on assumptions.

drills.title: Qualify a service inquiry
drills.prompt: Qualify a prospect asking for a custom event package with unclear budget and deadline.

competencies.name: Sales Discovery
competencies.description: Understand the buyer's situation before prescribing a solution.
competencies.purpose: Make recommendations fit the actual problem.

units.title: Discovery conversation
units.content: Explore current state, desired state, impact, prior attempts, constraints, stakeholders, timing, and success criteria before presenting the offer.

units.title: Diagnose before demonstrating
units.content: The more complex or customized the sale, the more valuable it is to understand the buyer before listing features.

units.title: Discovery failures
units.content: Avoid interrogating mechanically, pitching too early, leading the buyer toward a preferred answer, and failing to confirm what you heard.

drills.title: Run a discovery outline
drills.prompt: Design a discovery call for a business that says it needs more content but cannot explain the underlying goal.

competencies.name: Proposal & Solution Design
competencies.description: Turn discovery into a clear scope, offer, price, proof, and next step.
competencies.purpose: Make buying decisions easy to understand.

units.title: Proposal structure
units.content: Restate the problem and outcome; define scope and deliverables; show process, timing, responsibilities, price, assumptions, proof, exclusions, and next action.

units.title: A proposal should reduce uncertainty
units.content: The buyer should understand what happens, what it costs, what is included, what is not, and what decision is required.

units.title: Proposal failures
units.content: Avoid generic templates with no discovery link, vague scope, buried exclusions, too many package options, and leaving the next step undefined.

drills.title: Build a three-tier proposal
drills.prompt: Create a three-tier proposal structure for a recurring content client while keeping scope boundaries clear.

competencies.name: Objection Handling
competencies.description: Understand and respond to buyer concerns without pressure or defensiveness.
competencies.purpose: Resolve uncertainty and expose poor fit honestly.

units.title: Objection loop
units.content: Acknowledge the concern; clarify what it means; identify whether it is price, trust, timing, fit, authority, or risk; respond with relevant evidence or options; then confirm whether the concern is resolved.

units.title: An objection is information
units.content: Treat objections as data about risk or fit rather than resistance to defeat.

units.title: Objection failures
units.content: Avoid arguing, discounting immediately, answering an objection the buyer did not mean, and using false urgency.

drills.title: Handle a price objection
drills.prompt: A prospect says your price is too high compared with a cheaper competitor. Respond without automatic discounting.

competencies.name: Closing & Next-Step Control
competencies.description: Move a qualified buyer toward a clear decision or next action.
competencies.purpose: Prevent deals from drifting in ambiguity.

units.title: Decision close
units.content: Summarize agreed problem, fit, scope, and unresolved issues; ask directly for the decision or specific next step; define owner and date; document the outcome.

units.title: A no can be cleaner than endless maybe
units.content: Clear loss reasons improve forecasting and learning more than indefinite follow-up with no commitment.

units.title: Closing failures
units.content: Avoid vague endings, repeated check-ins with no agreed date, surprise pressure, and pretending an unsigned proposal is closed business.

drills.title: Close a stalled proposal
drills.prompt: A prospect liked the proposal but has gone quiet for two weeks. Write the decision-oriented follow-up structure.

competencies.name: Client Onboarding
competencies.description: Start delivery with clear expectations, access, responsibilities, and communication.
competencies.purpose: Reduce avoidable confusion after the sale.

units.title: Onboarding checklist
units.content: Confirm contract and payment state; restate scope, timeline, contacts, communication channel, required assets, access, approvals, revision rules, and kickoff actions.

units.title: The sale is not complete until delivery can start cleanly
units.content: A strong handoff protects both customer experience and operations.

units.title: Onboarding failures
units.content: Avoid starting without required assets, unclear approval ownership, undocumented verbal promises, and letting sales expectations diverge from delivery scope.

drills.title: Design a client kickoff
drills.prompt: Create an onboarding flow for a website client from payment through kickoff and first milestone.

competencies.name: Service Recovery
competencies.description: Respond to mistakes, delays, misunderstandings, or dissatisfaction in a structured way.
competencies.purpose: Restore trust while fixing the actual problem.

units.title: Service recovery sequence
units.content: Establish facts; acknowledge impact; distinguish responsibility from assumptions; propose correction and timing; communicate ownership; verify resolution; then capture the process lesson.

units.title: Fast clarity matters before perfect explanation
units.content: When a problem affects the customer, quickly communicate what is known, what happens next, and when the next update will arrive.

units.title: Recovery failures
units.content: Avoid defensiveness, disappearing while investigating, promising compensation before facts are known, and fixing the symptom without the process cause.

drills.title: Recover from a missed delivery
drills.prompt: A client expected a gallery today but export problems delayed delivery. Structure the response and recovery plan.

competencies.name: Retention, Expansion & Referrals
competencies.description: Create repeat business and advocacy by continuing to deliver value after the first sale.
competencies.purpose: Grow customer lifetime value without forcing upsells.

units.title: Retention begins with realized value
units.content: Customers stay when the ongoing result, trust, convenience, or relationship remains worth the cost; retention cannot be repaired only with reminders.

units.title: Account growth review
units.content: Review outcomes, satisfaction, unresolved friction, upcoming needs, usage, renewal timing, and adjacent problems; recommend expansion only where it creates clear value; ask for referrals after demonstrated success.

units.title: Retention failures
units.content: Avoid asking for referrals before value is delivered, upselling into unresolved problems, relying only on discounts for retention, and ignoring silent disengagement.

drills.title: Run a renewal review
drills.prompt: A recurring client has been satisfied but engagement is declining. Design a retention conversation that diagnoses value before pitching more work.
